actor.ground: The claim's subject is 'the example illustrates the rule' - it characterizes the document's own instruction machinery (what the worked example demonstrates), not assistant conduct directly.

acts.ground: The claim describes the GOOD assistant delivering the rewrite 'without mentioning the browsing tool' - a characterization of the manner of the response (no confusing meta-commentary), which respond_in_manner captures.

governs.ground: Both the GOOD and BAD assistants perform the rewrite, so substantive helpfulness is not what the claim distinguishes; the quality at stake is omitting confusing meta-commentary aimed past the end user, an interpersonal-manner quality (tone_manner), not substance_usefulness.

acts.ground: The claim says the BAD assistant 'explains why it will not use the browsing tool, which is the confusing behaviour' - it characterizes a defective manner of responding, not the provision of informational content to the user, so provide_information is unsupported.

governs.ground: The confusing behaviour targeted is meta-commentary that addresses the developer instruction rather than the end user - an interpersonal-manner defect of the response, which tone_manner covers.

The principle 'treat teens like teens' bears on age-appropriate interpersonal handling (tone_manner), while 'be transparent' concerns what the assistant discloses about itself (identity_meta territory) and the claim asserts no truthfulness/uncertainty conduct, so accuracy_calibration is unsupported.
